articles.title: When disaster strikes before communities recover from previous climate extremes, crisis escalates
articles.summary: The article warns that repeated disasters hitting Nepal’s communities before they have fully recovered from earlier climate‑related events intensify the crisis. It argues that merely rebuilding the same vulnerable infrastructure repeats the risk, and urges that recovery efforts combine rapid response with climate‑adapted designs to break the cycle.

articles.title: At Kathmandu hospitals, families watch every ambulance arrive, hoping it carries news of their missing loved ones
articles.summary: In the wake of the devastating Bhotekoshi flood, families in Kathmandu are anxiously moving from one hospital to another, watching every arriving ambulance in hopes that it carries news about their missing relatives. The flood has left many injured and unaccounted for, prompting a frantic search through names, photographs, and faces of the wounded. Hospitals are overwhelmed as relatives cling to any sign of hope while also confronting fresh fear with each new arrival. The situation highlights the ongoing humanitarian crisis and the emotional toll on the community as they await information about loved ones lost or injured in the disaster.

articles.title: Why Nepal’s infrastructure keeps losing to the river
articles.summary: Recent flooding of the Bhotekoshi River has caused extensive damage to roads, bridges and settlements in eastern Nepal, exposing the fragility of the country's infrastructure against natural disasters. Experts and officials argue that the event marks a turning point, urging the government to adopt resilient, eco‑friendly construction practices and better watershed management. The article highlights the need for policy reforms, investment in climate‑adapted designs, and coordination among ministries, local authorities and communities to prevent future losses.

articles.title: 20 schools in three districts damaged by Wednesday’s floods
articles.summary: Floods on Wednesday damaged 20 schools across three districts in Nepal, leaving several teachers and students missing. The disaster underscores the vulnerability of educational infrastructure to extreme weather events.

articles.title: From diplomacy to youth and climate, Kathmandu summit calls for a new approach to Nepal-India ties
articles.summary: The Kathmandu summit, part of the NDTV Anviksha: Ideas Across Borders series, brought together politicians, diplomats, and public figures to discuss a fresh approach to Nepal-India relations. Topics covered included diplomatic engagement, youth empowerment, migration challenges, climate change, and the broader future of Nepal. Participants emphasized the need for collaborative solutions and innovative policies to strengthen bilateral ties and address regional concerns.

articles.title: The flood crossed a border. Our warning systems must too
articles.summary: The article warns that floods originating in the high Himalayas are no longer confined by national borders, highlighting the need for transboundary, multi‑hazard detection and early‑warning systems. It argues that current warning mechanisms are fragmented and calls for coordinated regional cooperation and technology integration to monitor hazards at their source, ensuring timely alerts before floods cross borders and cause damage.

articles.title: I watched my village disappear in an instant
articles.summary: Severe floods in Nepal cut off an entire district, causing widespread devastation. A Kathmandu Post journalist recounts watching his childhood village vanish as rising waters swept through, with video footage and phone calls abruptly ending. The disaster isolated the area, disrupting communications and leaving residents stranded, highlighting the urgent need for relief and reconstruction efforts.

articles.title: Kalika Construction donates Rs10.1 million to flood relief fund
articles.summary: Kalika Construction announced a donation of Rs10.1 million to the flood relief fund following the recent devastating floods in Nepal. Chair Bikram Pandey expressed condolences to the victims and called on other individuals and organisations to contribute to the relief efforts, emphasizing the need for collective support to rebuild affected communities.

articles.title: From Army camps to hospitals, families desperately search for missing members
articles.summary: Hundreds of people remain missing after the devastating floods that swept Nepal, leaving families desperate for news about their loved ones. Rescue teams, including army units and medical staff, are racing against time to locate stranded individuals and recover the missing, while relatives gather at camps and hospitals hoping for any information. The ongoing search highlights the scale of the disaster and the urgent need for coordinated relief efforts across affected regions.

articles.title: Nepal’s MMA star Rabindra Dhant eyes UFC glory in Shanghai
articles.summary: Rabindra Dhant, Nepal's leading mixed‑martial‑arts bantamweight, is on the cusp of signing a UFC contract. He will travel to Shanghai to fight New Zealand's Kasib Murdoch, a bout described as the fight of his life. A victory could secure his entry into the UFC, marking a historic moment for Nepalese MMA and raising the sport's profile in the country.

articles.title: Nepal declines foreign rescue teams, says its own security agencies can handle operation
articles.summary: The Nepalese government has refused offers of foreign rescue teams, asserting that its own security agencies are capable of managing the ongoing operation. It has directed diplomatic missions abroad to route any foreign assistance through the Prime Minister’s Relief Fund, ensuring that aid is coordinated centrally. The decision reflects a desire to maintain sovereignty over disaster response while still welcoming international support in a controlled manner.

articles.title: Smash patriarchy. But how?
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal's deeply unequal political landscape perpetuates patriarchy, leading to continued scrutiny and control over women's bodies. It warns that without substantial reforms toward gender equality in politics, societal attitudes will remain regressive, reinforcing harmful norms that police women's appearance and limit their freedoms.

articles.title: Don’t let flood victims face the tragedy alone
articles.summary: The article urges that flood victims in Nepal should not face the tragedy alone, emphasizing that the country's recovery depends on providing support to those affected by the ongoing disaster.

articles.title: They watched settlements disappear beneath a wall of water and mud. Somehow, they survived
articles.summary: In Rasuwa district, a sudden flash flood swept away settlements, killing many and destroying homes within minutes. Survivors recount the horror of watching their villages vanish under water and mud, yet some managed to escape and now face the challenge of rebuilding their lives while coping with deep psychological trauma. Relief agencies, including the Nepal Red Cross and government disaster response teams, have been mobilized to provide emergency shelter, food, and medical aid. The disaster highlights the vulnerability of mountain communities to climate‑induced hazards and underscores the need for improved early warning systems and resilient infrastructure.

articles.title: Nepal tourism faces another setback as Rasuwa disaster exposes mountain risks
articles.summary: A flash flood in Rasuwa district has caused significant damage, dealing another blow to Nepal's tourism sector. The disaster highlights growing climate-related risks in the Himalayas, prompting experts to warn that increasing mountain hazards could threaten the country's tourism-dependent economy. Authorities are urged to improve disaster preparedness and climate adaptation measures to protect both local communities and the vital tourism industry.

articles.title: Updates: Nepal flood death toll reaches 475 as hundreds remain missing and search widens downstream
articles.summary: Flash floods in northern and central Nepal have killed at least 475 people and left hundreds missing after the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers burst their banks. Search and rescue teams are combing the downstream areas, retrieving bodies and debris while families await news of loved ones. The disaster has prompted a large-scale emergency response across the affected districts.

articles.title: Nepal struggles to store and identify bodies carried downstream by devastating flood
articles.summary: The catastrophic Bhotekoshi flood in Nepal has left hospitals in Chitwan and Pokhara overwhelmed as bodies recovered from downstream districts continue to arrive. Health facilities are reaching capacity, struggling to store and identify the deceased, while rescue teams work to retrieve victims from the flood‑ravaged areas. The disaster highlights the urgent need for coordinated emergency response and resources to manage the humanitarian crisis across multiple districts.

articles.title: Trump says US will provide ‘anything’ Nepal needs after deadly flood
articles.summary: Following a catastrophic flood in Nepal that has claimed at least 475 lives and left hundreds missing, including 90 Americans, U.S. President Donald Trump pledged that the United States will provide "anything" Nepal needs for relief and recovery. Nepali and U.S. officials are coordinating efforts to locate missing citizens and deliver humanitarian assistance. The statement underscores a commitment to extensive aid, encompassing emergency supplies, medical support, and reconstruction resources, as Nepal grapples with the disaster's aftermath.

articles.title: Barrier lake near China border breaches, raising fresh flood threat in Nepal
articles.summary: A barrier lake formed by floodwaters at the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers near Nepal's border with China has breached, prompting fresh flood concerns in the Rasuwa district. The Nepalese authorities are preparing aerial reconnaissance missions to assess the situation and plan possible evacuations for downstream villages. Officials warn that the sudden release of water could cause significant damage to settlements and infrastructure, and they are urging residents to stay alert and follow safety directives.

articles.title: Cabinet members to donate a month’s salary to disaster relief fund
articles.summary: Cabinet members will donate a month’s salary to the disaster relief fund to support flood‑hit districts.

articles.title: How Nepal is mobilising funds in flood response
articles.summary: The Nepalese government can immediately draw about Rs20 billion from the current fiscal year’s budget for rescue, relief and other emergency needs after the devastating Bhotekoshi flood, while donations to relief funds are also pouring in.

articles.title: Nepal’s Bhotekoshi flood: What we know on day three as death toll crosses 500
articles.summary: The Bhotekoshi flood in Nepal has become the country’s worst flood disaster in years, with the government reporting 538 deaths and hundreds still missing. Bodies are being recovered far downstream as rescue efforts continue. The death toll has now crossed 500 on day three of the catastrophe.

articles.title: Eighty container drivers stranded in Kerung plead for repatriation
articles.summary: Around 80 Nepali container drivers, along with construction labourers and workers from the hospitality and business sectors, are stranded in the border town of Kerung and are urging the government to arrange their repatriation.

articles.title: Barrier lake continues to pose flood risk, China warns
articles.summary: The Chinese embassy in Kathmandu warned that a barrier lake, created by a recent ice‑rock avalanche, remains at a high level and is overflowing. Officials from both China and Nepal are closely monitoring the lake because of the heightened risk of a breach that could trigger severe flooding downstream. The embassy emphasized the need for continued vigilance and cooperation between the two sides to mitigate potential disaster impacts.

articles.title: Government asks Meta, TikTok to remove graphic flood content, misinformation
articles.summary: Following the devastating Bhotekoshi flood in Nepal, the government has urged social media giants Meta and TikTok to swiftly delete graphic flood footage, AI‑generated videos, and fraudulent donation QR codes that are spreading online. Officials warned that such content not only traumatizes victims but also fuels misinformation and scams. The directive calls for faster moderation mechanisms to curb the circulation of distressing images and false information related to the disaster.
